newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RUGBY UNION-SEREVI VOWS TO RECOVER WORLD CUP SEVENS CROWN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SEREVI VOWS TO RECOVER WORLD CUP SEVENS CROWN.

text.p: Waisale Serevi, the uncrowned king of sevens rugby, vowed to help Fiji win the Rugby World Cup Sevens after they high-stepped past hapless Namibia on Saturday.

Playmaker Serevi, who flourishes in the wide open spaces of seven-a-side rugby, scored two tries and six conversions as Fiji put Namibia to the sword 66-0 in the opening pool A game of the second day.

Fiji have lost to New Zealand at the last three Hong Kong Sevens -- regarded as an unofficial world championship -- but they have power and pace in abundance in this tournament while the Kiwis have lost five of last year's winning side, including Jonah Lomu, Christian Cullen and Waisake Masirewa.

"I have made a promise back home in Fiji to bring back the Melrose Cup," said Serevi, the team captain who plays his club rugby in Japan. "I will try to keep true to that vow. We have started well but the quality of the teams is much higher than the Hong Kong Sevens and they all want to win."
South Africa, viewed as serious challengers for the Melrose Cup, upped the tempo from the largely meaningless first day, when the teams just played for ranking places, and defeated Ireland 34-7.
International flanker Andre Venter scored three tries in a match orchestrated by scrum-half Joost van der Westhuizen.

"We started today as if it was the first day of the tournament," said Westhuizen. "We have been training together for five weeks and the five experienced players in the side and the five youngsters are getting on well together as a unit. It's early days yet and I don't want to think about our prospects against Fiji or New Zealand."
New Zealand, in exactly the same pool as day one, beat Japan 47-0 but their usual rhythm was missing and skipper Eric Rush said they must improve before meeting Tonga later in the day.

Holders England, with a host of 15-a-side internationals in the squad, defeated Canada 30-7 with two tries from Jon Sleightholme and one apiece from Mike Catt, Chris Sheasby, Adedayo Adebayo and Neil Back.
Back said afterwards that England must improve markedly if they were to defend the Melrose Cup won at Murrayfield, Scotland, four years ago.
"We need to improve -- if we keep playing like this we are not going to be good enough," said Back. "It is all about ball retention and ours has not been that good."
Australia, runners-up in 1993, made hard work of beating Portugal 26-7 with two tries from international Damian Smith and one apiece from Wallaby backrower Michael Brial and John Moss.
They face Scotland, who they drew with 19-19 on Friday, in what could be a pool decider later in the day.
The first major shock to the tournament was delivered by hosts Hong Kong who beat Ireland 26-5 in pool B.

Hong Kong, hard hit by injuries on the first day, drafted in former Australian sevens winger Chris Gordon from a pool of replacements and he beefed up a side which already included former Tongan star Isi Tu'ivai and Vaughan Going, the nephew of All Black great Sid Going.
